passages.note: House Third Reading vote page on HB2853 (2022); Mathis voted N.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Bill text (Chapter 388, Sec. 2) adding the universal-eligibility provision that Mathis's No vote opposed.

rows.reasoning: Mathis's recorded No vote on HB2853 (2022) opposed the provision making "qualified student" include any resident eligible to enroll in a public school in any grade regardless of other eligibility criteria — the universal expansion matching "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school." A single No vote on this expansion shows opposition to universal eligibility but does not by itself separate the remaining rungs, so the row is BLANK direction-only.
needs_source: Mathis's own words (floor statement, press release, or questionnaire answer) explaining his No vote on HB2853 (2022), to determine whether he favors eliminating existing voucher programs, merely blocking further expansion, an income-capped program, or expansion short of universal.
